module purpose: neorv32_gptmr is a bus-accessible timer that stores control and threshold values, selects one clkgen_i bit as its tick source, counts until the count matches the threshold, and raises a pending interrupt. It also exports the enable state on clkgen_en_o and returns control, threshold, count, and pending-interrupt status through the bus response record.

use-case flows.value: timer enable bit and clock-source selection bits written into ctrl
timer threshold value written into timer.thres
stored enable state starting or stopping timer counting and interrupt generation
selected clkgen_i bit captured as timer.tick, timer.count updated, and match evaluated
interrupt-clear request bit latched and consumed to clear irq_pnd
pending interrupt state set on match and driven to irq_o
control bits, threshold, current count, and pending-interrupt status returned on bus reads
ctrl, timer.thres, irq_clr, timer.tick, timer.count, and irq_pnd forced to zero when rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.reasoning: Line 76 writes the enable bit into ctrl on a control-register write qualified by lines 73-75. That stored bit is exported on line 106, forces timer.count to zero when low on lines 118-119, and qualifies irq_pnd update on lines 141-148. Integrity is established because timer start/stop behavior, exported enable, and interrupt suppression all depend on this bit being correct; availability is established because ctrl holds it between writes and reset line 63 clears it deterministically. The bus request/response ports are transport records, so only the internal register and scalar output are listed.

Lines 77-79 write the three selection bits into ctrl on a control-register write, and line 117 uses ctrl(ctrl_prsc2_c downto ctrl_prsc0_c) as the index selecting which clkgen_i bit becomes timer.tick. Integrity is established because the selected tick source determines the counter update cadence and therefore later match and interrupt behavior; availability is established because the stored selection is reused on every timer_core cycle until rewritten or reset at line 63. Readback exists on lines 90-92, but bus_rsp_o is a transport record, so only ctrl is listed.

Line 84 stores timer.thres on threshold-register writes qualified by lines 73-74 and 83, line 131 compares it against timer.count to form timer.match, and line 96 returns it on bus reads. Integrity is established because changing timer.thres changes when match occurs and thus when the counter resets and irq_pnd sets at lines 121-123 and 142-143. Availability is established because the register holds the value between writes and presents it to the comparator each cycle; the bus read exit is omitted because bus_rsp_o is transport.

timer.count is cleared by reset at line 115, by disable at line 119, and by match at line 122, and otherwise increments from itself at line 124 when timer.tick = '1' at line 120. Line 131 consumes the stored count in the match comparison and line 98 returns it on bus reads. Integrity is established because correct timer operation depends on exact count progression; availability is established under the RTL-visible conditions that with ctrl enabled and timer.tick asserted, the register advances, while explicit reset, disable, and match branches force it to zero.

Line 131 computes timer.match from the equality of timer.count and timer.thres; the map records timer.match CONSTRAINED_BY timer.count and timer.thres at occurrence 3. That decision resets timer.count at lines 121-122 and sets irq_pnd at lines 142-143, so integrity is established for rollover and interrupt timing. Availability is established because the comparison is continuously formed from the stored operands.

irq_pnd is set to '1' on match while enabled at lines 141-143, cleared by irq_clr when enabled and no simultaneous match at lines 144-145, and forced to '0' when disabled or reset at lines 138-139 and 147-148. Line 154 exports the state on irq_o and line 94 exposes it on bus reads. Integrity is established because the reported interrupt state must follow these set/clear rules exactly; availability is established because a qualifying match produces a pending interrupt and the state remains asserted until one of the explicit clear conditions occurs.

irq_clr is forced to '0' at reset and at the start of each bus_access cycle on lines 65 and 71, then loaded from the control-write data bit at line 81. irq_generator consumes it at lines 144-145 to clear irq_pnd when enabled and when no simultaneous match has higher priority. Integrity is established because this one-cycle clear event directly controls whether a pending interrupt is removed; availability is established because a qualifying write produces the clear pulse for the next irq_generator edge. The write source is bus_req_i, a transport record, so only the internal latch is listed.
